title: I'd like to invite you
goal: Invite Sēf to dinner at your flat, and say yes warmly when he asks you a favour
tip: ḥabbēt is a polite 'I'd like to'. Put a bare present verb after it, as after abi: ḥabbēt aʿazmak 'I'd like to invite you', ḥabbēt aṭbakh 'I'd like to cook'. It sounds softer than abi, and a woman says it the same way.
dialogue: B
هلا سيف! حبيت أعزمك على العشا يوم الخميس
hala Sēf! ḥabbēt aʿazmak ʿala l-ʿasha yōm il-khamīs
Hi Sēf! I'd like to invite you to dinner on Thursday.
هَلَا سَيْفْ! حَبَّيْتْ أَعَزْمَكْ عَلَى الْعَشَا يَوْمْ الْخَمِيسْ
A
هلا فيك! على هالخشم. وين العزيمة؟
hala fīk! ʿala hal-khashim. wēn il-ʿazīma?
Hi! With pleasure. Where's the dinner?
هَلَا فِيكْ! عَلَى هَالْخَشِمْ. وَيْنْ الْعَزِيمَة؟
B
في شقتي. وفهد والشباب؟ قول لهم، الله يخليك
fi shiggati. w Fahad w ish-shabāb? gūl-lhum, allāh ykhallīk
At my flat. And Fahad and the guys? Tell them, please.
فِي شِقَّتِي. وْفَهَدْ وْالشَّبَابْ؟ قُولْ لْهُمْ، اللّٰهْ يْخَلِّيكْ
A
أبشر! بس سوي لنا كرك مثل ما تسويه أمي
abshir! bas sawwī-lna karak mithil ma tsawwīh ummi
You got it! But make us karak the way my mum makes it.
أَبْشِرْ! بَسْ سَوِّي لْنَا كَرَكْ مِثِلْ مَا تْسَوِّيهْ أُمِّي
B
على راسي! وحبيت أطبخ لكم أكل بريطاني
ʿala rāsi! w ḥabbēt aṭbakh-lkum akil brīṭāni
Gladly! And I'd like to cook you (all) some British food.
عَلَى رَاسِي! وْحَبَّيْتْ أَطْبَخْ لْكُمْ أَكِلْ بْرِيطَانِي
A
أكل بريطاني؟ إن شاء الله ريحته حلوة!
akil brīṭāni? in shāʼ allāh rīḥtah ḥilwa!
British food? Let's hope it smells good!
أَكِلْ بْرِيطَانِي؟ إِنْ شَاءْ اللّٰهْ رِيحْتَهْ حِلْوَة!
items: I'd like to (+ verb), I wanted to (polite)
use it before a verb: ḥabbēt agūl-lak = I wanted to tell you; a woman says the same; on its own ḥabbēt can mean 'I loved' or 'I kissed'
I'd like to invite you (to a man)
to a woman: ḥabbēt aʿazmich (حبيت أعزمج)
the invitation; the dinner or lunch you're invited to
with pleasure, gladly (lit. on this nose)
a warm yes to an invitation or a favour
you got it, consider it done (to a man)
to a woman: abshiri (أبشري); the answer to a request, to friends and elders alike
to a woman the same: sawwī-lna
gladly, at your service (lit. on my head)
the answer to a favour someone asks of you
culture: Gulf hosts insist, often with wallāh. To turn something down politely, say mashkūr, allāh ykhallīk, or il-marra l-yāya 'next time'. To say yes to an invitation or a favour, ʿala hal-khashim and ʿala rāsi are warm, very Gulf answers.

title: I'd love to, but…
goal: Maryam invites you to lunch with the team: say you'd love to, explain why you may be late, and ask for the address
tip: widdi + a bare verb is 'I'd love to': widdi ashūf il-jamāʿa 'I'd love to see everyone'. It's softer than abi, so it's good for a kind no: widdi wallāh, bas… 'I'd really love to, but…'. To ask: widdak? to a man, widdich? to a woman.
grammar: widdi + verb 'I'd love to'; widdak? 'would you like to?'
dialogue: A
باكر بنتغدى كلنا مع بعض. ودك تيي؟
bāchir binitghadda killna maʿa baʿaẓ. widdak tiyi?
Tomorrow we're all having lunch together. Would you like to come?
بَاكِرْ بِنِتْغَدَّى كِلّْنَا مَعَ بَعَضْ. وِدَّكْ تِيِي؟
B
ودي والله، بس عندي محاضرة الساعة ثنتين
widdi wallāh, bas ʿindi muḥāẓra s-sāʿa thintēn
I'd really love to, but I've got a lecture at two.
وِدِّي وَاللّٰهْ، بَسْ عِنْدِي مُحَاضْرَة السَّاعَة ثِنْتَيْنْ
A
خسارة! وبعد المحاضرة؟ نحن في المطعم اللي صوب المكتب
khasāra! w baʿd il-muḥāẓra? niḥin fi l-maṭʿam illi ṣōb il-maktab
Shame! What about after the lecture? We'll be at the restaurant near the office.
خَسَارَة! وْبَعْدْ الْمُحَاضْرَة؟ نِحِنْ فِي الْمَطْعَمْ اللِّي صَوْبْ الْمَكْتَبْ
B
إن شاء الله. ودي أشوف الجماعة كلهم
in shāʼ allāh. widdi ashūf il-jamāʿa killhum
God willing. I'd love to see everyone.
إِنْ شَاءْ اللّٰهْ. وِدِّي أَشُوفْ الْجَمَاعَة كِلّْهُمْ
A
إن شاء الله يعني هيه، ولّا يعني لا؟
in shāʼ allāh yaʿni hē, walla yaʿni la?
Does 'in shāʼ allāh' mean yes, or does it mean no?
إِنْ شَاءْ اللّٰهْ يَعْنِي هَيْه، وَلَّا يَعْنِي لَا؟
B
يعني هيه! بس يمكن أتأخر. تطرشين لي العنوان؟
yaʿni hē! bas yimkin atʼakhkhar. tṭarrshīn-li l-ʿinwān?
It means yes! But I might be late. Will you send me the address?
يَعْنِي هَيْه! بَسْ يِمْكِنْ أَتْأَخَّرْ. تْطَرّْشِينْ لِي الْعِنْوَانْ؟
A
أكيد. وما عليه، نترياك!
akīd. w ma ʿalēh, nitrayyāk!
Of course. And don't worry, we'll wait for you!
أَكِيدْ. وْمَا عَلَيْهْ، نِتْرَيَّاكْ!
items: a kind way to say no
would you like to…? (to a man)
to a woman: widdich…? (ودج…؟); widdak tiyi? = would you like to come?
widdi ashūfak = I'd love to see you
it means yes, I mean yes
will you send me (to a woman)
we'll wait for you (to a man)
culture: in shāʼ allāh 'God willing' goes with every plan, and people mean it. It can also be a polite, non-committal 'maybe'. So if you really mean yes, add something firm: in shāʼ allāh, akīd 'definitely', or name a time.

title: Let's go to the desert
goal: Suggest a desert trip to Sēf, ask if you can bring a friend, and ask to come back early
tip: khal + a we-verb is a quick 'let's': khal nrūḥ 'let's go', khal nshūf 'let's see'. It means the same as khallna nrūḥ. yṣīr? asks 'is it OK?': yṣīr ayīb rbīʿi? 'can I bring my friend?'. The answer is yṣīr 'it's fine' or ma yṣīr 'no, it's not OK'.
dialogue: A
يوم السبت شو نسوي؟
yōm is-sabt shu nsawwi?
What shall we do on Saturday?
يَوْمْ السَّبْتْ شُو نْسَوِّي؟
B
خل نروح البر! الجو حلو هالأيام
khal nrūḥ il-barr! il-jaww ḥilu hal-ayyām
Let's go to the desert! The weather's nice these days.
خَلْ نْرُوحْ الْبَرّْ! الْجَوّْ حِلُو هَالْأَيَّامْ
A
والله فكرة! خل نقول للجماعة بعد
wallāh fikra! khal ngūl lil-jamāʿa baʿad
Good idea! Let's tell the others too.
وَاللّٰهْ فِكْرَة! خَلْ نْقُولْ لِلْجَمَاعَة بَعَدْ
B
زين. ويصير أييب ربيعي مارك؟
zēn. w yṣīr ayīb rbīʿi Mārk?
Great. And is it OK if I bring my friend Mark?
زَيْنْ. وْيْصِيرْ أَيِيبْ رْبِيعِي مَارْكْ؟
A
يصير! أكيد، في مكان في السيارة
yṣīr! akīd, fī makān fi s-sayyāra
Sure, of course! There's room in the car.
يْصِيرْ! أَكِيدْ، فِي مَكَانْ فِي السَّيَّارَة
B
وحبيت أسألك: يصير نرجع بدري؟ لازم أذاكر
w ḥabbēt asʼalak: yṣīr nirjaʿ badri? lāzim adhākir
And I wanted to ask: can we come back early? I have to revise.
وْحَبَّيْتْ أَسْأَلَكْ: يْصِيرْ نِرْجَعْ بَدْرِي؟ لَازِمْ أَذَاكِرْ
A
ما يصير! بس ما عليه، خل نشوف. يمكن الساعة عشر
ma yṣīr! bas ma ʿalēh, khal nshūf. yimkin is-sāʿa ʿashr
No way! But OK, let's see. Maybe at ten.
مَا يْصِيرْ! بَسْ مَا عَلَيْهْ، خَلْ نْشُوفْ. يِمْكِنْ السَّاعَة عَشْرْ
items: khal ngūl l-Fahad = let's tell Fahad
is it OK? can I? can we?
yṣīr ayīb…? = can I bring…?; answer: yṣīr, or ma yṣīr
no, it's not OK; that won't do
with friends it can also be a joking 'no way!'
ma fī makān = there's no room
I have to revise, I have to study

title: Let's finish it first
goal: Plan the afternoon with Maryam at the office, then suggest karak to the whole team
tip: khallna 'let's' changes with who you talk to: khallīna to a woman, khallūna to a group. The next verb takes n- for 'we': khallūna niṭlaʿ 'let's head out' (to a group). You'll also hear khallīna said to men.
grammar: khallīna (to a woman), khallūna (to a group) + verb
dialogue: A
سالم، المدير يبي الملف اليوم!
Sālim, il-mudīr yabi l-malaff il-yōm!
Sālim, the manager wants the file today!
سَالِمْ، الْمُدِيرْ يَبِي الْمَلَفّْ الْيَوْمْ!
B
زين، خلينا نخلص قبل الغدا
zēn, khallīna nkhalliṣ gabil il-ghada
OK, let's finish before lunch.
زَيْنْ، خَلِّينَا نْخَلِّصْ قَبِلْ الْغَدَا
A
خلنا نبدا الحين. أنا أكتب وانت تطالعه
khallna nibda l-ḥīn. ana aktib w inta tṭālʿah
Let's start now. I'll write and you look it over.
خَلّْنَا نِبْدَا الْحِينْ. أَنَا أَكْتِبْ وْاِنْتَ تْطَالْعَهْ
B
أوكي. وبعد الشغل نشرب كرك كلنا؟
ōkē. w baʿd ish-shughul nishrab karak killna?
OK. And after work, shall we all have karak?
أَوْكَيْ. وْبَعْدْ الشُّغُلْ نِشْرَبْ كَرَكْ كِلّْنَا؟
A
فكرة حلوة! خل نقول للجماعة كلهم
fikra ḥilwa! khal ngūl lil-jamāʿa killhum
Nice idea! Let's tell the whole team.
فِكْرَة حِلْوَة! خَلْ نْقُولْ لِلْجَمَاعَة كِلّْهُمْ
B
يا جماعة! خلونا نطلع الساعة خمس. يصير؟
yā jamāʿa! khallūna niṭlaʿ is-sāʿa khams. yṣīr?
Everyone! Let's head out at five. OK?
يَا جَمَاعَة! خَلُّونَا نِطْلَعْ السَّاعَة خَمْسْ. يْصِيرْ؟
A
بس أول خلنا نخلص الملف!
bas awwal khallna nkhalliṣ il-malaff!
But first let's finish the file!
بَسْ أَوَّلْ خَلّْنَا نْخَلِّصْ الْمَلَفّْ!
items: to a man: khallna (خلنا); to a group: khallūna (خلونا); you'll also hear khallīna said to men
to one man: khallna; to one woman: khallīna
to a man: khallna nkhalliṣ; nkhallṣah = we finish it
let's head out, let's go out (to a group)
to one man: khallna niṭlaʿ; to one woman: khallīna niṭlaʿ

title: Checkpoint 2.4: lunch at Bū Rāshid's
goal: Bū Rāshid phones to invite you to Friday lunch: answer respectfully, ask to bring Fahad, and promise not to be late
tip: With an elder, stay respectful: yā ʿammi, ṭāl ʿumrak, and abshir for 'consider it done'. For a group, -kum and -ūn come back: killkum 'all of you', la titʼakhkharūn 'don't be late', nshūfkum 'we'll see you all'. widdna is 'we'd love to'.
grammar: checkpoint 2.4: recycle s2u055–s2u071 (elders, invitations, ḥabbēt, widdi, yṣīr)
dialogue: A
السلام عليكم يا سالم. شحالك؟
as-salāmu ʿalaykum yā Sālim. shḥālak?
Peace be upon you, Sālim. How are you?
السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَا سَالِمْ. شْحَالَكْ؟
B
وعليكم السلام! بخير الله يسلمك. شحالك يا عمي؟
wa ʿalaykum is-salām! b-khēr allāh ysallmak. shḥālak yā ʿammi?
And upon you! Fine, thank you. How are you, sir?
وَعَلَيْكُمْ السَّلَامْ! بْخَيْرْ اللّٰهْ يْسَلّْمَكْ. شْحَالَكْ يَا عَمِّي؟
A
الحمد لله. حبيت أعزمك على الغدا يوم الجمعة
il-ḥamdu lillāh. ḥabbēt aʿazmak ʿala l-ghada yōm il-jumʿa
Thank God. I'd like to invite you to lunch on Friday.
الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهْ. حَبَّيْتْ أَعَزْمَكْ عَلَى الْغَدَا يَوْمْ الْجُمْعَة
B
على هالخشم! يصير أييب فهد وياي؟
ʿala hal-khashim! yṣīr ayīb Fahad wiyyāy?
With pleasure! May I bring Fahad with me?
عَلَى هَالْخَشِمْ! يْصِيرْ أَيِيبْ فَهَدْ وِيَّايْ؟
A
أكيد! تعالوا كلكم، بس لا تتأخرون
akīd! taʿālu killkum, bas la titʼakhkharūn
Of course! Come, all of you, just don't be late.
أَكِيدْ! تَعَالُوا كِلّْكُمْ، بَسْ لَا تِتْأَخَّرُونْ
B
أبشر طال عمرك! ودنا نشوفك
abshir ṭāl ʿumrak! widdna nshūfak
Of course, sir! We'd love to see you.
أَبْشِرْ طَالْ عُمْرَكْ! وِدّْنَا نْشُوفَكْ
A
الله يحفظكم. نشوفكم يوم الجمعة إن شاء الله
allāh yiḥfaẓkum. nshūfkum yōm il-jumʿa in shāʼ allāh
God keep you all. See you all on Friday, God willing.
اللّٰهْ يِحْفَظْكُمْ. نْشُوفْكُمْ يَوْمْ الْجُمْعَة إِنْ شَاءْ اللّٰهْ
items: to one man: la titʼakhkhar; to one woman: la titʼakhkharīn
consider it done, sir (respectful) (to a man)
to a woman: abshiri ṭāl ʿumrich (أبشري طال عمرج); to an elder or someone senior
we'd love to see you (to a man)
to a woman: widdna nshūfich (ودنا نشوفج); widdna + verb = we'd love to
God keep you all (warm thanks or goodbye) (to a group)
to one man: allāh yiḥfaẓak; to one woman: allāh yiḥfaẓich (الله يحفظج)
we'll see you all, see you (to a group)
to one man: nshūfak; to one woman: nshūfich

title: Are you upset?
goal: Maryam looks upset at work: ask what's wrong and cheer her up
tip: Feeling words agree with the person: zaʿlān (a man), zaʿlāna (a woman). With kān they go into the past: kint zaʿlāna 'I was upset' (a woman). illi links a verb to a noun: il-ʿarẓ illi sawwētah 'the presentation I did'. ṣij? is 'really?'.
grammar: recycle: kān + feeling word; illi + verb
dialogue: A
صباح الخير
ṣabāḥ il-khēr
Good morning.
صَبَاحْ الْخَيْرْ
B
صباح النور! خير؟ انتي زعلانة؟
ṣabāḥ in-nūr! khēr? inti zaʿlāna?
Good morning! Everything OK? Are you upset?
صَبَاحْ النُّورْ! خَيْرْ؟ اِنْتِي زَعْلَانَة؟
A
هيه شوي. المدير ما عجبه العرض اللي سويته
hē shwayy. il-mudīr ma ʿajabah il-ʿarẓ illi sawwētah
A bit, yes. The manager didn't like the presentation I did.
هَيْه شْوَيّْ. الْمُدِيرْ مَا عَجَبَهْ الْعَرْضْ اللِّي سَوَّيْتَهْ
B
صج؟ بس العرض كان حلو! أنا عجبني
ṣij? bas il-ʿarẓ kān ḥilu! ana ʿajabni
Really? But the presentation was good! I liked it.
صِجْ؟ بَسْ الْعَرْضْ كَانْ حِلُو! أَنَا عَجَبْنِي
A
والله؟ أنا كنت زعلانة من الصبح
wallāh? ana kint zaʿlāna min iṣ-ṣubḥ
Really? I was upset all morning.
وَاللّٰهْ؟ أَنَا كِنْتْ زَعْلَانَة مِنْ الصُّبْحْ
B
ما عليه، لا تزعلين. يمكن المدير كان تعبان
ma ʿalēh, la tizʿalīn. yimkin il-mudīr kān taʿbān
Never mind, don't be upset. Maybe the manager was tired.
مَا عَلَيْهْ، لَا تِزْعَلِينْ. يِمْكِنْ الْمُدِيرْ كَانْ تَعْبَانْ
A
يمكن. الحين أحسن. يلا، نبدا الشغل قبل الغدا
yimkin. il-ḥīn aḥsan. yalla, nibda sh-shughul gabil il-ghada
Maybe. I feel better now. Come on, let's get some work done before lunch.
يِمْكِنْ. الْحِينْ أَحْسَنْ. يَلَّا، نِبْدَا الشُّغُلْ قَبِلْ الْغَدَا
items: a woman: zaʿlāna (زعلانة); zaʿlān min = upset with
to a man: la tizʿal (لا تزعل)
he didn't like it (lit. it didn't please him)
she didn't like it: ma ʿajabha (ما عجبها); I liked it: ʿajabni (عجبني)
that I did; that you did (to a man), after a noun
to a woman: illi sawwētīh (اللي سويتيه); il-ʿarẓ illi sawwētah = the presentation I did

title: Calm down!
goal: Sēf is angry in the car park: calm him down and find out what's really wrong
tip: Use kān and illi to say what's behind a feeling: il-imtiḥān illi kān ams 'the exam (that was) yesterday'. mʿaṣṣib is 'angry' (a woman: mʿaṣṣba). allāh yihdāk 'God guide you' is a gentle 'come on now' to a friend who's overdoing it.
dialogue: A
شوف هذا! خذ مكاني! ما صارت!
shūf hādha! khadh makāni! ma ṣārat!
Look at him! He took my spot! This is too much!
شُوفْ هٰذَا! خَذْ مَكَانِي! مَا صَارَتْ!
B
لا تعصب يا ريّال. خل نشوف، في مكان ثاني هناك
la tʿaṣṣib yā rayyāl. khal nshūf, fī makān thāni hnāk
Calm down, mate. Let's see, there's another spot over there.
لَا تْعَصِّبْ يَا رَيَّالْ. خَلْ نْشُوفْ، فِي مَكَانْ ثَانِي هْنَاكْ
A
كل يوم جي! أنا معصب من الصبح
kill yōm chī! ana mʿaṣṣib min iṣ-ṣubḥ
It's like this every day! I've been angry since this morning.
كِلّْ يَوْمْ جِي! أَنَا مْعَصِّبْ مِنْ الصُّبْحْ
B
ليش معصب؟ شو اللي صار؟
lēsh mʿaṣṣib? shu illi ṣār?
Why are you angry? What happened?
لَيْشْ مْعَصِّبْ؟ شُو اللِّي صَارْ؟
A
الامتحان اللي كان أمس، ما نجحت فيه. وايد زعلان
il-imtiḥān illi kān ams, ma nijaḥt fīh. wāyid zaʿlān
The exam yesterday: I didn't pass it. I'm really upset.
الْاِمْتِحَانْ اللِّي كَانْ أَمْسْ، مَا نِجَحْتْ فِيهْ. وَايِدْ زَعْلَانْ
B
الله يهداك! امتحان واحد بس. المرة الياية إن شاء الله
allāh yihdāk! imtiḥān wāḥid bas. il-marra l-yāya in shāʼ allāh
Come on now! It's just one exam. Next time, God willing.
اللّٰهْ يِهْدَاكْ! اِمْتِحَانْ وَاحِدْ بَسْ. الْمَرَّة الْيَايَة إِنْ شَاءْ اللّٰهْ
A
صح كلامك. خلاص، ما بعصب
ṣaḥḥ kalāmak. khalāṣ, ma baʿaṣṣib
You're right. OK, I won't get angry.
صَحّْ كَلَامَكْ. خَلَاصْ، مَا بَعَصِّبْ
items: calm down, don't get angry (to a man)
to a woman: la tʿaṣṣbīn (لا تعصبين)
why are you angry? (to a man)
this is too much! this has gone too far!
said when something keeps happening or someone overdoes it
come on now (gentle telling-off, lit. God guide you) (to a man)
to a woman: allāh yihdāch (الله يهداج)
a woman says the same; to a man: ma bitʿaṣṣib? = you won't get angry?
to a woman: ṣaḥḥ kalāmich (صح كلامج)

title: I was scared, now I'm happy
goal: Tell Sēf how your presentation went: how nervous you were and how happy you are now
tip: kint + a feeling word is 'I was …': kint khāyif 'I was scared'. The word agrees with the person: khāyif / khāyfa, mistānis / mistānsa. khāyif min is 'scared of'; khāyif ʿala is 'worried about (someone)'.
dialogue: A
شو صار في العرض اللي سويته اليوم؟
shu ṣār fi l-ʿarẓ illi sawwētah il-yōm?
How did the presentation you gave today go?
شُو صَارْ فِي الْعَرْضْ اللِّي سَوَّيْتَهْ الْيَوْمْ؟
B
كنت خايف من المدير، بس العرض كان زين!
kint khāyif min il-mudīr, bas il-ʿarẓ kān zēn!
I was scared of the manager, but the presentation went well!
كِنْتْ خَايِفْ مِنْ الْمُدِيرْ، بَسْ الْعَرْضْ كَانْ زَيْنْ!
A
قلت لك: لا تخاف! وشو قال المدير؟
gilt-lak: la tkhāf! w shu gāl il-mudīr?
I told you: don't worry! And what did the manager say?
قِلْتْ لَكْ: لَا تْخَافْ! وْشُو قَالْ الْمُدِيرْ؟
B
قال: حلو وايد! والله وايد مستانس
gāl: ḥilu wāyid! wallāh wāyid mistānis
He said: really nice! I'm so happy.
قَالْ: حِلُو وَايِدْ! وَاللّٰهْ وَايِدْ مِسْتَانِسْ
A
صج؟ مبروك! الليلة العشا على حسابي
ṣij? mabrūk! il-lēla l-ʿasha ʿala ḥsābi
Really? Congratulations! Tonight dinner's on me.
صِجْ؟ مَبْرُوكْ! اللَّيْلَة الْعَشَا عَلَى حْسَابِي
B
الله يبارك فيك! وانت بعد كنت خايف علي؟
allāh ybārik fīk! w inta baʿad kint khāyif ʿalay?
Thanks! And were you worried about me too?
اللّٰهْ يْبَارِكْ فِيكْ! وْاِنْتَ بَعَدْ كِنْتْ خَايِفْ عَلَيْ؟
A
شوي! بس الحين أحسن، وأنا بعد مستانس
shwayy! bas il-ḥīn aḥsan, w ana baʿad mistānis
A bit! But it's all fine now, and I'm happy too.
شْوَيّْ! بَسْ الْحِينْ أَحْسَنْ، وْأَنَا بَعَدْ مِسْتَانِسْ
items: I was scared; you were scared (to a man)
a woman says: kint khāyfa; to a woman: kinti khāyfa
don't worry, don't be scared (to a man)
to a woman: la tkhāfīn (لا تخافين)
happy, pleased, having a good time (a man)
what did she say?: shu gālat?
a woman: khāyfa ʿalay (خايفة علي); khāyif ʿalēk = worried about you

title: Khēba!
goal: Sēf teases you about your big meal: tease him back the way friends do
tip: Friends tease, and the replies are short: khēba! 'seriously?!' to poke fun, ḥarām ʿalēk! 'that's not fair!' to protest, amzaḥ wiyyāk 'I'm joking'. kān still helps: hādhāk kān ghada 'that was lunch'.
dialogue: A
خيبة! بتاكل كل هذا؟
khēba! bitākil kill hādha?
Seriously?! You're going to eat all that?
خَيْبَة! بِتَاكِلْ كِلّْ هٰذَا؟
B
حرام عليك! ما كليت شي من الصبح
ḥarām ʿalēk! ma kalēt shay min iṣ-ṣubḥ
That's not fair! I haven't eaten anything since this morning.
حَرَامْ عَلَيْكْ! مَا كَلَيْتْ شَيْ مِنْ الصُّبْحْ
A
أمزح وياك! لا تعصب. بالعافية
amzaḥ wiyyāk! la tʿaṣṣib. bil-ʿāfya
I'm joking! Don't get cross. Enjoy your food.
أَمْزَحْ وِيَّاكْ! لَا تْعَصِّبْ. بِالْعَافْيَة
B
الله يعافيك. وانت أمس كليت صحنين!
allāh yʿāfīk. w inta ams kalēt ṣaḥnēn!
Thanks. And you ate two plates yesterday!
اللّٰهْ يْعَافِيكْ. وْاِنْتَ أَمْسْ كَلَيْتْ صَحْنَيْنْ!
A
تمزح؟ هذاك كان غدا وعشا!
timzaḥ? hādhāk kān ghada w ʿasha!
Are you kidding? That was lunch and dinner!
تِمْزَحْ؟ هٰذَاكْ كَانْ غَدَا وْعَشَا!
B
خيبة! يلا، خلني آكل قبل لا يبرد
khēba! yalla, khallni ākil gabil la yibrad
Seriously?! Come on, let me eat before it gets cold.
خَيْبَة! يَلَّا، خَلّْنِي آكِلْ قَبِلْ لَا يِبْرَدْ
A
صح كلامك! يصير آكل وياك؟
ṣaḥḥ kalāmak! yṣīr ākil wiyyāk?
You're right! Can I eat with you?
صَحّْ كَلَامَكْ! يْصِيرْ آكِلْ وِيَّاكْ؟
items: pokes fun at someone overdoing it, or sounds unimpressed; never with strangers or elders
that's not fair! come on! (to a man)
to a woman: ḥarām ʿalēch (حرام عليج)
to a woman: amzaḥ wiyyāch (أمزح وياج)
you're going to eat all that? (to a man)
to a woman: bitāklīn kill hādha? (بتاكلين كل هذا؟); said with khēba to tease
can I eat with you? (to a man)
to a woman: yṣīr ākil wiyyāch? (يصير آكل وياج؟)
culture: Friends in the Gulf tease each other a lot, and khēba 'seriously?!' is part of it: it pokes fun at someone overdoing it (khēba, you'll eat all that?) or says you're not impressed. Keep it for friends your own age: with strangers or elders it can sound rude.
